cockpit.bannerTitle: Today is the pulse of the workspace
cockpit.bannerBody: See health, live activity and model spend in one place before you dive into threads or agents.
cockpit.intro: Start here when you want to know whether work is flowing and where attention is needed.

sections.title: Today
sections.body: Cards show open work, pending decisions, agent runs and custom KPIs. Use this tab to scan the day, then jump into Communication or Agenda from the attention items.

sections.title: Activity
sections.body: A combined timeline of agent runs and human actions (status changes, assignments, invites). Filter by agents or people when you need to audit what happened.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Model spend and volume against the workspace budget. Caps live here so operators can raise or pause spend without leaving the cockpit.

communication.bannerBody: Customer messages, agent chats and internal threads share one inbox. Connect channels, then reply or let AI draft answers.
communication.runsBannerBody: Scheduled scans and agent updates live here. Items waiting on a yes or no sit under Decisions.
communication.decisionsBannerBody: Every open approval — customer drafts and internal agent asks — lives here. Approve or edit on the thread card.
communication.intro: The hub for every conversation — external customers and internal agents in one place.

sections.title: Inbox queues
sections.body: Open is customer work that is still waiting. Scheduled holds conversations with a date. Pin important threads, assign owners, and plan what can wait.

sections.title: Channels
sections.body: Email, webchat, WhatsApp and Slack each get a queue when connected. Channel settings and AI reply modes live under Settings in the sidebar.

sections.title: Agents in threads
sections.body: Mention an agent or start a chat from New conversation. Agent runs and decision cards appear inline — approve or edit before anything goes out.

sections.title: Decisions
sections.body: Open DecisionRequests from any channel share the Needs decision filter on the inbox. Today For you and notification clicks open the same list.

contacts.bannerTitle: Contacts are the people behind your threads
contacts.bannerBody: Everyone who writes in — email, chat or other channels — lands here so the team can recognize, approve and group them.
contacts.intro: A shared address book built from real conversations, not a separate CRM you have to keep in sync.

sections.title: People and companies
sections.body: Switch between people and companies. Link contacts to a company so related threads stay grouped. Use Link contacts if older threads never received a company.

sections.title: Approve and block
sections.body: New addresses can wait for approval. Approved contacts stay in the book; blocked senders drop out of normal handling.

sections.title: Open the conversation
sections.body: From a contact you jump back into their threads in Communication. The contact record is the person; the inbox is the work.

agenda.bannerTitle: Agenda is the clock of the workspace
agenda.bannerBody: What happened, what happens now and what is planned, for people and agents, next to your own calendars.
agenda.intro: One timeline for connected calendars, tasks (one-off or recurring, for people and agents) and activity.

sections.title: Day, week, month and list
sections.body: Switch views at the top right. Use the arrows or the mini month to move in time. Click an empty slot in Day or Week to plan a task.

sections.title: Show and who
sections.body: Under Show, turn on each connected calendar plus Tasks and Activity. Filter on one person, one agent or one folder.

sections.title: Tasks
sections.body: One-off wakes, recurring scans and stage follow-ups from flows are all Tasks. Due tasks show under For you. Manage recurring scans under Manage tasks.

sections.title: Calendar sync
sections.body: Connect Google Calendar or Outlook Calendar under Connections. Each connected calendar has its own checkbox. Agents can propose new blocks that wait for your approval.

agents.bannerTitle: Agents are the team that does the work
agents.bannerBody: Create and configure the AI workers for this workspace. Chat with them, give them tools, and point them at folders.
agents.intro: The library of people-shaped AI workers. Communication is where they talk; this page is where you hire and brief them.

sections.title: Library
sections.body: Every agent is a card. The default handler has a Lead badge. Open a card to change instructions, model, tools and chat access.

sections.title: Chat and schedule
sections.body: Chat opens an internal thread with that agent. Schedule jumps to Agenda filtered to the same agent so you can attach a wake.

sections.title: New agent
sections.body: Admins add agents from New agent. Members can talk to existing agents from Communication. Tool access and autonomy still follow Govern.

projects.bannerBody: Group a product-owner agent, repository, threads and a token budget so work has a home instead of living only in chat.
projects.intro: A folder is the container for a goal: who leads it, which repo it uses, and how much it may spend.

sections.title: Cards
sections.body: Each folder shows its lead agent, repo status and remaining budget. Open it for orchestration, repository and recent runs.

sections.title: Threads
sections.body: View threads deep-links into Communication filtered to that folder. Agents and humans keep talking in Communication; the folder is the spine.

sections.title: Budget
sections.body: Daily and hourly token budgets sit on the folder so a single goal cannot consume the whole workspace cap.

knowledge.bannerBody: Persona, memory, skills and checklists live as workspace docs. Agents read them on every run and can write back what they learn.
knowledge.intro: Markdown files the workspace owns. This is the brief agents carry — not a separate wiki for humans only.

sections.title: Kinds
sections.body: Persona is tone and rules. Memory is long-term facts. Skills are procedures (SKILL.md style). Heartbeat and daily log are AI-maintained checklists.

sections.title: Publish
sections.body: Mark a doc published to expose it on the public help center for this tenant. Internal drafts stay in the workspace only.

sections.title: Search and write
sections.body: Search is hybrid (keywords + embeddings). Agents use the same docs through tools. Edits you make here are live on the next run.

govern.bannerBody: Set how autonomous agents may be, review drafts, and lock tools that should never run without you.
govern.intro: Structural change and risk live here. Day-to-day replies stay in Communication; this page is policy.

sections.title: Autonomy posture
sections.body: Manual, assisted or autonomous presets change default apply modes and tool allowances for the whole workspace.

sections.title: Drafts and decisions
sections.body: Agent-proposed platform changes wait here until someone accepts or rejects them. Inline decisions in threads are for message-level choices; Govern is for lasting policy.

sections.title: Tools
sections.body: Per-category sliders (deny, ask, allow) plus per-tool overrides. External customer sessions never auto-mutate, regardless of posture.

channels.bannerBody: Connect a mailbox first. Website chat, WhatsApp and Slack each get a queue when they are connected.
channels.intro: Bring customer mail and other inboxes into Communication so work lands in one place.

integrations.bannerTitle: Connections are the tools agents may call
integrations.bannerBody: Install catalog apps and MCP servers, then set on Govern whether agents may use them automatically.
integrations.intro: Give agents tools outside Bokito — accounting, GitHub, MCP servers and catalog apps.

models.bannerTitle: Models decide what the workspace can call
models.bannerBody: Enable chat and embedding models here. Spend still shows on Today Usage; Govern still decides what agents may do.
models.intro: Pick which language and embedding models this workspace may use, and who pays for them.

widget.bannerTitle: The website widget lands in Communication
widget.bannerBody: Install the snippet on your site. Visitor chats appear next to email in the same hub.
widget.intro: Put Bokito chat on your site so visitors land in the same Communication hub as email.

autonomy.bannerTitle: Autonomy is the workspace trust dial
autonomy.bannerBody: Manual, assisted or autonomous presets change how much agents may do before a person steps in.
autonomy.intro: Dial how much agents may do on their own, from full oversight to exception-only review.

categories.bannerTitle: A label has a flow only while that flow is attached
categories.bannerBody: Each conversation can carry one label. Filing it makes the conversation a ticket that moves through the flow's stages, on one of its folders or on none.
categories.pageTitle: How a label with a flow works
categories.intro: A label with a flow turns a conversation into a ticket, like a complaint or a refund request. One list, read by people and agents alike.

sections.title: One per conversation
sections.body: A conversation carries at most one label with a flow. Other labels sit next to it and never start a flow.

sections.title: Read first, confirm when unsure
sections.body: Bokito reads every inbound message against this list. A certain match files a ticket; an unsure match asks for a confirm on the thread.

sections.title: Flow and folder
sections.body: The linked Flow holds the stages, owners and check-ups. Filing settles a folder: one of the flow's folders, or none.

sections.title: Backlog
sections.body: Requests that keep arriving without a match land in the backlog. Attach a flow when it is worth tracking.

recurringWake.promptDefault: Take a short look at how the workspace stands: channels, connections, flows and labels with a flow, folders, agents, and what keeps coming back in conversations. Name what is open and waiting on me. Then suggest at most three concrete steps that move the workspace forward, for example a flow for a question that comes back often, a folder for work that now sits loose in conversations, or a catalog integration that fits what we do. Say why for each step, and offer to set it up for me once I agree. Do not repeat a suggestion that is still open or that I turned down.

aiTools.body: Use this workspace's governed tools from the AI tool you already work in. OAuth signs in through the browser; an app token is the fallback for scripts and CI.
aiTools.tokenHint: Create a token under App tokens below and the snippets fill it in. Until then they show YOUR_BOKITO_API_TOKEN.

cursor.name: Cursor
cursor.description: Use Bokito tools in Cursor's agent.
cursor.body: Cursor signs in with OAuth: paste the URL and approve in the browser. Use a token only for setups that cannot open a browser.
cursor.oauth1: Open Cursor Settings, then MCP, and add a server.
cursor.oauth2: Paste the JSON below. It holds only the URL, no token.
cursor.oauth3: Save. Cursor opens the browser: sign in to Bokito and pick a workspace.
cursor.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.
cursor.token2: Paste the JSON below into Cursor Settings, then MCP.
cursor.token3: Save. The tools that token allows appear for the agent.

claudeCode.name: Claude Code
claudeCode.description: Add Bokito to the Claude Code CLI.
claudeCode.body: Claude Code supports OAuth for remote MCP servers. Add the server once for your user, then sign in from inside Claude Code.
claudeCode.oauth1: Run the command below in a terminal.
claudeCode.oauth3: Choose bokito, then Authenticate. Sign in to Bokito in the browser and pick a workspace.
claudeCode.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.
claudeCode.token2: Run the command below. Claude Code sends the token on every call.

claudeDesktop.name: Claude Desktop
claudeDesktop.description: Add Bokito as a custom connector in Claude.
claudeDesktop.body: Claude adds remote servers as connectors in its settings, with OAuth. Its JSON config only runs local servers, so the token route uses the mcp-remote bridge.
claudeDesktop.oauth1: In Claude, open Settings, then Connectors, and choose Add custom connector.
claudeDesktop.oauth3: Choose Connect, sign in to Bokito and pick a workspace. Claude connects from Anthropic's servers, so this needs a public Bokito address.
claudeDesktop.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.
claudeDesktop.token2: Open claude_desktop_config.json from Settings, then Developer, and paste the config below. The mcp-remote bridge needs Node.js.
claudeDesktop.token3: Restart Claude Desktop and check that the Bokito tools load.

codex.name: Codex CLI
codex.description: Add Bokito to the OpenAI Codex CLI.
codex.body: Codex reads MCP servers from config.toml. It signs in with OAuth, or reads a token from an environment variable so the token stays out of the file.
codex.oauth2: Run codex mcp login bokito and sign in to Bokito in the browser.
codex.oauth3: Start Codex. The Bokito tools are listed under /mcp.
codex.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.
codex.token2: Set BOKITO_MCP_TOKEN in the shell where Codex runs, with the first line below.

vscode.name: VS Code
vscode.description: Use Bokito in Copilot agent mode.
vscode.body: VS Code reads MCP servers from mcp.json and offers them to Copilot in agent mode. It signs in with OAuth, or asks for a token once.
vscode.oauth1: Create .vscode/mcp.json in your folder, or run MCP: Open User Configuration.
vscode.oauth2: Paste the JSON below and save.
vscode.oauth3: Choose Start above the server entry. VS Code opens the browser to sign in to Bokito.
vscode.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.
vscode.token3: Choose Start and paste the token when VS Code asks. It keeps the token in its secret storage.

windsurf.name: Windsurf
windsurf.body: Windsurf reads remote MCP servers from mcp_config.json. It signs in with OAuth, or reads a token from an environment variable.
windsurf.oauth1: In Windsurf, open the MCP settings and choose to edit mcp_config.json.
windsurf.oauth2: Paste the JSON below and save.
windsurf.oauth3: Refresh the servers. Windsurf opens the browser to sign in to Bokito.
windsurf.token1: Create an app token under App tokens below.
windsurf.token2: Set BOKITO_MCP_TOKEN in the environment Windsurf starts from, with the first line below.
windsurf.token3: Paste the JSON into mcp_config.json and refresh the servers.

chatgpt.name: ChatGPT
chatgpt.description: Add Bokito as an app in ChatGPT developer mode.
chatgpt.body: ChatGPT connects remote MCP servers as apps in developer mode. It supports OAuth only, so there is no token route.
chatgpt.oauth1: In ChatGPT, open Settings, then Apps, then Advanced settings, and turn on Developer mode.
chatgpt.oauth2: Choose Create app and enter {{url}} as the server URL.
chatgpt.oauth3: Pick OAuth as the authentication and save.
chatgpt.oauth4: Sign in to Bokito and pick a workspace. ChatGPT connects from OpenAI's servers, so this needs a public Bokito address.

generic.name: Any MCP client
generic.description: Call the MCP endpoint from scripts or CI.
generic.body: Any client that speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP can use the endpoint with an app token. Governed tools still ask when policy requires it.
generic.token1: POST JSON-RPC to {{url}} with Authorization: Bearer and your token.
generic.token2: Call tools/list, then tools/call with the same token.
generic.token3: A token with scopes only sees those tool categories. No scopes means every tool.

workbench.title: Hand work to a coding tool
workbench.body: Hand a bug or feature from a conversation to a coding tool. Connect your own API key; Bokito starts the job, shows progress in the thread, and brings the pull request back.
workbench.phase1: Available now. Uses your own provider account.
workbench.phase2: Planned after the Bokito GitHub App, which brings pull request status and issue sync.
workbench.phase3: Planned with the local relay for your own machine.

cursorAgents.name: Cursor Cloud Agents
cursorAgents.description: Cursor runs the job in the cloud and opens a pull request.
cursorAgents.body: Bokito starts a Cursor cloud agent on your repository with the brief from the conversation, streams its progress into the thread, and passes your answers back while it runs. You connect your own Cursor API key.

claudeManaged.name: Claude Managed Agents
claudeManaged.description: Claude works the job in an Anthropic-hosted sandbox.
claudeManaged.body: Bokito starts a Claude session on your repository with the brief from the conversation, streams its progress into the thread, and stops it at the budget you set. You connect your own Anthropic API key.

devin.name: Devin
devin.description: Devin works the task in its own environment.
devin.body: Bokito starts a Devin session, shows its questions as decisions in the thread, and stops it at the budget you set. You connect your own Devin service user key.

copilot.name: GitHub Copilot cloud agent
copilot.description: Copilot works on a task in your GitHub repository.
copilot.body: Bokito starts a Copilot task in your repository as the person who approved it. Follow-ups go through pull request comments. Needs the Bokito GitHub App.

claudeCodeCi.name: Claude Code in GitHub Actions
claudeCodeCi.description: Claude Code runs in your own GitHub Actions.
claudeCodeCi.body: Bokito proposes a workflow for your repository, then starts it per job with the brief. The job runs on your Actions minutes with your own Anthropic key.
